notes.title: Playtest Update 5
notes.content:
[p]Player controls and information
[/p][list][*][p] Time acceleration can be increased by pressing  the period key ( . ) and decreased by pressing the comma key ( , ) . This is an additional option for players without a keypad. The keys + and – still work for players with a keypad.
[/p][/*][*][p] The player's view is fixed when activating the selection mode in first person view, instead of following the ship's oscillation. This makes it easier to click on another ship when using the the spy glass (some players indicated it was too difficult to click on far ships due to the player ship's oscillation)
[/p][/*][*][p] Depth sounding now provides fraction of a fathom. Depth feedback now uses the historical language: "a quarter less five" (4.75) or "and a half three" ( 3.5). The officer will also warn when there are few inches of water between the keel and the sea bottom [/p][/*][*][p] More feedback from the officers according to the players actions (e.g. „Steady as she goes“ when activating the helmsman) [/p][/*][*][p] When following a route at the highest speed now the ship will properly reach the waypoints. Until now sometimes the ship could „overshoot“ a waypoint and try to turn back to go to the waypoint
[/p][/*][*][p] Number of cannons is shown properly after repairs
[/p][/*][*][p] Bow chaser battery will now shoot the same projectile type as the other batteries (only starboard/larboard batteries were changing ammo type when requested, bow chaser was shooting only cannon balls) [/p][/*][*][p] Clicking on a ship when the pointer is highlighted will now always open a panel even if type is not known (shown as “Unknown vessel”) or no interactions are possible. Previously, no panel would open, making it feel like a bug (several player reports in this direction) [/p][/*][/list][p]
NPC improvements
[/p][list][*][p] NPCs will consider the ship speed to decide if tacking is possible or wearing is the better option
[/p][/*][*][p] NPCs will finish tacking manoeuvres before trying to change tack again (NPCs would often interrupt the tacking manoeuvre to change direction and stay trapped in irons)
[/p][/*][*][p] Improved use of the sails for some ships to support the tacking manouver
[/p][/*][*][p] NPCs will manoeuvre to avoid collision when following routes
[/p][/*][*][p] NPCs can look for protection of nearby coastal defences
[/p][/*][*][p] Update of physical data of other ships than the 9 pdr frigate for better ship handling (e.g. weight increased, burden was giving too low weight, making the tacking more difficult)
[/p][/*][*][p] More decisive and efficient algorithm when NPC turn the ship to  point at a target
[/p][/*][*][p] NPCs will intercept their target by extrapolating the target's speed instead of sailing to the target's current position [/p][/*][*][p] NPC will avoid running aground better when fleeing from an enemy (change of direction still too aggressive when close to the coast, but this will be improved)[/p][/*][*][p] NPCs will send their marines to the tops in battle too [/p][/*][/list][p]
Physics and mechanics
[/p][list][*][p] When the ship hits rocks at high speed a leak is generated
[/p][/*][*][p] Carronades have now a lower muzzle speed than cannons and therefore a lower range, to match the historical performance of carronades
[/p][/*][*][p] Cannon balls/bar shot/grapeshot now have realistic deceleration under water (higher than before). This reduces the likelihood of hits below the waterline and reduces the probability of ships sinking.
[/p][/*][*][p] Improved coordination of crew setting and furling sails. Previously, several sails could be crewed by a single seaman, waiting for another to be available to complete the job. With small crews (e.g. after a ship was captured) this could lead to a deadlock, where sails could not be set (all seamen waiting for somebody else)
[/p][/*][*][p] Probability of killing crew by smaller projectiles and splinters is reduced to achieve more realistic injured/killed ratio (matching historical action reports)
[/p][/*][*][p] Deploying boats now reduce the mass of the ship (first step towards mechanic to make your ship lighter to get free in case of running aground) [/p][/*][/list][p]
Worldbuilding
[/p][list][*][p] New ship type as NPC sailing in the world (make a cruise and find out ;-) … hope to see soon the first picture posted)
[/p][/*][*][p] Anchorages St Helens and Torbay added
[/p][/*][*][p] Lighthouses are visible now from farther distances (specially the lighthouse at Ushant was disappearing too soon)
[/p][/*][*][p] New land batteries located at the historical positions of „Corps the Garde“ (guardhouses) along the french coast for increased coverage of the coast defences [/p][/*][/list][p]
Miscellaneous
[/p][list][*][p] Eliminated the „blinking“ of the cannons (as one player described it)
[/p][/*][*][p] CPU load caused by rendering sailors reduced by 40% [/p][/*][*][p] Pinnace boat added to the 9pdr frigate (such a ship could have 4-5 boats, not only 2 as was the case until now)[/p][/*][*][p]Time of day dropdown sets time properly again (bugfix)[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45543657/4f670c1bf5322ccf4ef4a56a452496d9f52a8cd9.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Playtest update 4
notes.content:
Stil some control improvements:

[list]
[*] New separate control for the the bow chaser battery. Now it can be control independently by pressing the space bar (same logic as the larboard and starboard batteries). 
[*] Decoupled the manual adjustment sliders of the yards from the any lateral movement (A/D or arrows in first person view). Before the last clicked slider would react to any lateral movement inputs, as long as the player didn't click the mouse again (default setting from the engine)
[*] Added Fire at Will information to the gun battery UI, so players can identify they have ordered this mode. Shown as FAW (Fire At Will) when the target in the view area of that battery.
[*] Plymouth Dockyard is now separate port (independent from Plymouth) so players can anchor directly in front on the dockyard.
[*] Increased force of the anchor rope / capstan when weighing anchor (review showed higher force was physically possible) . This makes the weighing maneuver easier (wind forces or rudder action could would deviate the bow before)
[*] Surrendered enemies will now be able to take their sails (as long as crew is still alive), but still stop fighting. Before all actions by enemy crew would be deactivated, some ships leaving the sails set and still moving
[*] Boat 2 (yawl) can now capture all the ships again (before it was only working with the merchant schooner)
[*] Number of seriously injured crew members and dead are properly displayed in the log 
[*] Cannonballs, grapeshot, bar-shot have now also a probability of only injuring (e.g. limb lost) instead of only killing. Still lower probability than musket fire, canister shot or flying wood splinters.
[*] Improvement of crew management for the case that an order to the crew was cancelled before crew members reached their position
[*] Corrections to the release crew from battery buttons (one wrong binding, were also not appearing if the player selected a target via menu and didn't beat to quarters)
[*] Added button in the main menu to open the game guide in Steam (so new players can find it faster)
[*] Control information added to the guide
[/list]

notes.title: Playtest update 3
notes.content:
First I want to thank all the playtesters providing feedback and (action) reports in the in-game report tool or in the discussion forum in Steam. This information is very helpful to decide the topics which need work and work priorities.
The list of changes in this update is mostly based on the player's feedback

[list]
[*]NPC interaction panel now adds the description of the vessel and indicates "No actions available" when this is applicable. There are cases where interactions with another ship are not available (e.g. allied or neutral merchant ships or a surrendered enemy vessel when no boats are available to capture it and the player is too far away).  There were several reports of not being able to interact (e.g. not panel displayed or only an empty panel)
The vessel description (except allied/neutral/enemy) will match the map description i.e. when a ship is too far away, nationality is not provided yet to the player.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45543657/a6a1c164ba78c741d578288e1e8c8ecb5114007e.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45543657/56da4dce6389d816a758afa838ad09223570991b.png[/img][/url]
Interactions available with new description on top

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45543657/6883a52ec0cffc9302beb6b18dd18cad7fb18f55.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45543657/ba83af6059fc09898a5c96851f695b0c3af79533.png[/img][/url]
No interactions available due to being an allied merchant

[*]New gun battery information UI to help players understand the behaviour of the batteries and the state of the guns (cannons, carronades). There were several reports of the batteries not firing and it was difficult to know when it was due to any unexpected behaviour of the simulation or due to commands different to the player expectations (i.e. battery was aiming to a different target than what the player wanted to shoot at). 
This panel appears on the upper right corner only when at least a battery is crewed. The projectile selection list is still separate and below; this UI is a first implementation to be able to understand better your reports and will be improved (e.g. include the selection of projectiles in the battery UI as symbols)

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45543657/7a9796c2309ff349aeeef857da5200855951d926.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45543657/1255bc16b7d958807aff5e1f1945bab39d135ac0.png[/img][/url]

First line represents the bow chasers, second the quarterdeck carronades (left and right), the third line the upper deck cannons (left and right). In each battery you can see first the number of cannons ready to fire (i.e. loaded and with crew), second the number of cannons operational (i.e. will be reduced when cannons are damaged) Then the target identification and optional information (not in view for that battery, our of range)

[*]Officers provide now information about water ingress because of damage below the waterline: when it starts, when it's serious enough to start using the pumps (player can decide any time) and when the water flow is so high that the water level keeps rising even when the pumps are active. This should remind and help the players decide to activate the pumps. A further damage report is in the roadmap (I really like how in the Master and Commander film the carpenter Mr Lamb reports the amount of water in the hold to Captain Aubrey as "2 feet 6 inches ... and holding")  
[*]Repairs at port now include also repair of the rudder, replacement of damaged guns and replacement of lost anchors.
[*]Cutting of an anchor is now also possible during the process of weighing it, if the player decides it's taking too long (e.g. enemy approaching, rough weather). Before the weighing of the anchor could not be interrupted to cut the anchor
[*]New command to stop the pumps if these are started. Useful if the player needs the crew for the sails and the guns more urgently.
[*]Increased traversing speed for carronades and smaller cannons. Original turning speed was appropriate to bigger guns (e.g. 32pdr cannons) but smaller guns and specially carronades by design should be easier to traverse. Should make more likely to the guns to point to the target and being able to shoot (guns will shoot when hitting the target is possible)
[*]Master will keep the same sail when given the command to trim only the sails. There was a case of a unsubordinated master adding/reducing sails against the captain orders (master was court-martialed ;P)
[*]Reduction of effect of grapeshot at reducing enemy short-term morale. Before the number of hits had more importance than damage to the hull i.e. how many splinters were flying around (leading to very fast surrender of enemy crews) . Now if the grapeshot doesn't pierce the hull, there is no morale effect (no splinters flying around to scare the crew). For sure grapeshot disabling crew or cannons have the same effect
[*]Increase drag for projectiles in the water to limit the velocity and likelihood of projectiles piercing the hull. Action reports show high number of sunk vessels. Comparison of physical calculation with the engine simulation of drag showed projectiles had a too high speed in water, piercing hulls more easily. Further improvement in the future (engine uses "linear" drag, real drag should be quadratic with speed)
[*]NPC ships now offer a bigger surface to click and open the interaction menu  when seen from behind. Sails were only used to detect the mouse when seen from the front. From the rear view of the ship sails were not detected, so the player needed to click on the hull (confusing if on some situations clicking on the sails was feasible
[*]Corrections to boat behaviour when collecting and deploying these. Now also collection is only possible when the boat is close to the ship again (need to request first the boat to come close to the ship) There were some cases of boats not functional after a first deployment
[*]Prized captured by the boats will now be displayed in the log too (before only the prizes taken directly by the players ship were written down)
[*]Corrections to crew not fulfilling functions (e.g. set or take sails, use the cannons, moving on deck) after a time acceleration phase
[*]Further corrections of NPC navigation error (i.e. sailing north) when the ship was trying to reach a far point out of the navigation support.
[*] Messages from your officers will now stay in accelerated time as long as in normal time scale (messages were disappearing as the time acceleration
[*]"Leave Guns" command was renamed to "Release crew" and separated in starboard and larboard. Crew doesn't necessarily leave the guns immediately but can stay if no other tasks are given (e.g. use the other battery) or the time is not accelerated (idle crew will return below deck after certain time acceleration. There were reports of crews not leaving the guns
[*]Separate command to the officers to "Store cannons". Cannons will be stored in the ship, so gun ports  can be closed. Will be important when sailing in rough seas to avoid water ingress through the gun ports (needs to be implemented)
[*]Port names of "Le Havre" and "St-Nazaire" corrected
[/list]

notes.title: Playtest update 2
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Correction of error causing of NPC ships losing navigation (i.e. Sailing always north instead of engaging o fleeing properly) after long travel of the player after start. Now the navigation support updates properly as the player sails long distances. Sometimes you will notice some slow down of the simulation during the update (this will be improved).
[*] New memory management for all the terrain chuncks. Faster initial loading and less RAM memory used. Hope to solve issues by some players when starting the game or players with tight RAM resources. Will also allow to include the complete map in the future (as shown in the store page, including the mediterranean sea)
[*] Added new ship type roaming in the world (was visible in the „Museum“ but not being spawned)
[*] Fort at Portmouth now correctly bahving as british fort (was configured as spanish and could fire at the player depending on the date)
[*] Increased pump performance to make it more likely to reach port for repairs (in the future some emergency repairs need to be added)
[*] Repairs at friendly port lead also to sail repairs (until now only hull was repaired, missing crew recovered; repair was possible at any port, even enemy).
[*] Feedback by officers when the ships hit the sea bottom i.e. water to shallow (player were reporting the ship getting stuck as a bug)
[*] Feedback by officers when player gives fire order to battery not manned
[*] UI hides the option to collect a boat when the player is also on a boat (boats cannot collect other boats). Player needs to board the ship before collecting other boats. Before some unexpected behavior was possible (crew of collected boat would disspear but no collection) when the player tried to collect an NPC boat from another boat.
[*] UI provides feedback that „No anchor actions“ are possible (e.g. all anchors cut). Before the UI would show a small square but no explanation, when an action was requested, but no anchor was available for that action.
[*] Bow chasers travers angle increased to make it more likely that these can shoot at ships in front of the player's ship (before these could not point straight ahead and the player needed more steering to make it possible).
[*]Corrected visual glitch where bow chasers would clearly change smoothnes when approaching from a long distance (LOD)
[*] Several corrections to internal exceptions which can trigger unexpected behavior of the simulation (e.g. several cases whe an enemy ship was surrendering)
[*] Decoupled the F12 key (used for taking pictures when running under Steam) from a development function to change the weather (player would trigger a weather change when taking a picture)
[*] Added to the manual the control to request to the ship master „Heaving to“ (was always there, only description missing; only relevant when ship master is enabled)
[/list]

notes.title: First update with fixes for playtest
notes.content:
- White surface appearing at sea level between Saint Malo and Granvile is disabled now
- Building being visible through the fog in Portsmouth dockyard solved (setting for material corrected)
- Position of buttons for report corrected. At least one user reported with an ultrawide monitor that the buttons were overlapping with the messages from the officers
- Boat 1 (launch) now responds properly to rudder commands (before the boat would turn to the opposite direct to the request)
- Corrected exception error when coastal batteries update the nationality information
